To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the weak or intermediate-coupling shell-model can be reformulated in such a way, that no matrix elements of two-body interactions appear in the equations.
the weak and intermediate coupling model can be formulated as an eigenvalue problem in a space spanned by a subspace of the full shell-model space.

the secular equations of the shell-model weak or intermediate coupling approach to 2p — 1h states can be rewritten as simultaneous coupling of a (ph) and a (pp) Tamm-Dancoff vibration and that the new formulation has a number of advantages over the usual one.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new formulation of the weak coupling model which is free of the usual drawbacks of the usual shell model approach and which can be applied to a wider range of problems.
the mathematical properties of a new shell-model approach to the 2p-1h states and with a numerical application.

the following questions: (i) What is the relation between the usual shell-model secular equation and the simultaneous coupling of the two TDA subsolutions? (ii) What is the effect on the spectrum if the usual shell-model equations are replaced by our new ones?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new formulation of the weak coupling model does not lead to any improvement over the usual formulation.
all the different approaches to the 2 particle —1 hole states give the same result for the low lying states of O17.
the new approach to the weak or inter-mediate coupling model is numerically superior to the usual one, but it has to be applied with some caution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the usual shell model approach is equivalent to the weak coupling model in which a particle is coupled to a (ph) vibration and a hole to a particle-hole (ph) vibration.
the new approach is more transparent and more easily applicable.
the new formulation of the weak coupling model is numerically superior to the usual shell model approach and that it is also more transparent and easier to handle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the usual shell model approach to 2(p) — 1(h) states is mathematically not equivalent to the weak coupling model.
the new formulation of the weak coupling model is more efficient in the sense that it requires less computational resources.
the new approach is numerically more stable and that the secular equations are more easily diagonalised than the standard ones.
